extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for planning and preparing successful project funding proposals for community programs, covering strategic planning, proposal components, submission logistics, budgeting, and appendices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessing needs
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess needs using empirical data collection, common sources of statistical data, and data analysis and interpretation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guide emphasizes collecting empirical evidence to document community needs, identifying standard data sources, and analyzing/interpreting data to justify the proposed project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Developing strategies
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop strategies as part of strategic planning prior to writing the proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use assessed needs to design program strategies that are feasible, targeted, and linked to measurable outcomes; strategic planning is an explicit preparatory step before drafting the proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obtaining local support
rubrics_metrics.description: Obtain local support for the proposed project from relevant stakeholders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guide recommends securing buy-in from local organizations, partners, and community leaders to strengthen credibility and demonstrate community backing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determining possibilities of renewal
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine the possibilities of renewal or ongoing funding when planning the proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether the project can be sustained or renewed beyond the grant period and describe plans or prospects for renewal to funders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Getting expert advice / technical assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: Seek expert advice and technical assistance during proposal preparation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify and consult experts or technical assistance sources to improve proposal quality, methodology, evaluation design, and budget accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Locating funding sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Locate appropriate funding sources, including government agencies, corporations, and foundations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research funders' priorities and eligibility; match your project goals to likely funders and maintain a list of potential agencies and foundations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selecting proper funding agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Select the proper funding agencies to which to submit the proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose funders whose missions, program areas, and grant mechanisms align with your project; selecting the right agency increases fit and funding chances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: Time proposals appropriately with respect to funder deadlines and program cycles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan submission timelines to meet deadlines, allow for internal review and revisions, and align with funders' budgeting and decision cycles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identifying contacts / decision makers
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify relevant contacts and decision makers at funding agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Locate program officers, reviewers, or staff who manage grants to obtain information, clarify fit, and ensure the proposal is routed correctly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tracking contacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Track contacts and communications with funders and partners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain records of outreach, responses, submission confirmations, and follow-ups to manage the application process and relationships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal writing tips (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow general proposal writing tips provided in the guide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 3 begins with a list of practical tips for writing proposals—these cover clarity, organization, persuasiveness, and presentation (the guide describes these tips in context).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover letter
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a cover letter as a component of the proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guide describes the cover letter's role—concise introduction, point of contact, and summary of the request—to frame the proposal for reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary (executive summary)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a clear summary of the proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summaries should succinctly present the problem, objectives, methods, expected outcomes, and funding request to give reviewers an immediate understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduction
rubrics_metrics.description: Write an introduction that situates the project and organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the introduction to present organizational background, mission, capacity, and how the proposed project fits into broader goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a problem statement that defines the need your project addresses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Problem statements should be evidence-based, clearly articulated, and tied to the assessed needs data to justify the intervention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: State clear, measurable objectives for the proposed project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Objectives should be specific, measurable, achievable, relevant, and time-bound (SMART) and linked to evaluation measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the methodology for accomplishing project objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain activities, timelines, responsible parties, and methods; justify chosen approaches and demonstrate feasibility and rigor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Include an evaluation plan to assess project outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outline evaluation questions, indicators, data collection and analysis methods, responsible evaluators, and how findings will inform future work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete, well-structured budget
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare a complete, well-structured budget covering all necessary costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part 4 explains essential budget elements and emphasizes clarity and accuracy so funders can see how funds will be used and justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typical line item costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Include typical line item costs in the budget (personnel, supplies, equipment, travel, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Break down costs into standard line items so reviewers can evaluate reasonableness and necessity of each expense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matching share (cost sharing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Address the concept of matching share or cost sharing in the budget.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify any required or proposed matching contributions (cash or in-kind) and how they will be documented and sustained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cash flow
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider cash flow implications in budget preparation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan for timing of expenses and reimbursements to ensure the project can operate without funding gaps; present realistic cash flow assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Future funding / sustainability
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan for future funding and project sustainability beyond the grant period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe plans to continue or sustain activities after the grant (e.g., additional funders, earned income), and include these considerations in the budget narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Include typical elements in the proposal appendix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part 5 lists common appendix materials (e.g., resumes, letters of support, organizational documents, additional data) that support the main proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of funding information and technical assistance resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Consult annotated bibliographies and electronic resources for funding information and technical assistance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guide concludes with an annotated bibliography of 61 sources to help grantseekers locate funding information, technical assistance guides, and electronic resources.
